paragraphs: In Bury you can foster with the council's own team, Foster with Bury, or with one of the independent agencies listed above. The council is one of the ten Greater Manchester councils behind Foster for Greater Manchester, the joint campaign that represents nearly 1,500 mainstream foster carers across the city region.

Bury says it particularly needs carers for brothers and sisters who need to stay together, and for older children and young people. Its options range from full-time short-term and long-term fostering to regular respite, day care and occasional sleepovers, so there is room for people who cannot offer a full-time placement. Fostering is open to people of any age, gender, relationship status or sexual orientation.

For its approved mainstream carers the council lists a 50% council tax discount, which it says is available regardless of where you live, professional allowances that reflect your skills and the child's age, extra payments for birthdays, festivals and holidays, paid respite each year, mileage and essential equipment. Training and support groups are held locally, there are family events and day trips, and carers can join the Mockingbird programme, in which an experienced hub carer supports a small group of fostering households. The council does not publish its weekly rates on these pages, so ask for them.

Bury Council is also a Fostering Friendly employer under The Fostering Network's scheme, giving staff who foster, or who are being assessed, at least five extra days of paid leave. During Foster Care Fortnight in May 2026 its team held drop-in sessions at the Fostering Hub in Bury Town Hall. Speak to the council and two or three services above before choosing, and see the Rochdale, Bolton, Salford and Manchester pages if you live near the borough's boundary.
